# Incident Report — Koi Stealer Infection (2024-09-04)

## 1. Victim Host

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **172.17.0.99** |
| MAC address | **18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4** (vendor prefix Intel) |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-RNVO9AT** |
| AD domain | BEPOSITIVE.COM (DC: WIN-CTL9XBQ9Y19.bepositive.com, 172.17.0.17) |
| Logged-in Windows user | **afletcher** (observed in Kerberos AS-REQ `CNameString` = `afletcher`, realm `BEPOSITIVE.COM`) |

Confirmed via DHCP (Option 12 hostname `DESKTOP-RNVO9AT` tied to MAC `18:3d:a2:b6:8d:c4`, IP `172.17.0.99`), NBNS name registration, and Kerberos ticket traffic.

## 2. Malware Family

**Koi Stealer** (Win32/Koi Stealer). **Signature-confirmed**, not behavioral guesswork: Suricata/ET rule fired directly on the traffic — `ETPRO TROJAN Win32/Koi Stealer CnC Checkin (POST) M2` (48 hits, 172.17.0.99 → 79.124.78.197). This is corroborated by the actual wire content: the beacon POSTs use a distinctive pipe-delimited payload format (`101|<GUID>|<campaign-id>|<base64 blob>`, e.g. `101|30168213-3be0-a751-81a0-cf3b228c8654|5LHtVruc|f3f3oMg2lz4XGyHy0LidzFiNvSftke//k+COyrO9aBI=`) sent as `Content-Type: application/octet-stream` with a legacy MSIE 7.0/Windows-NT-10.0 spoofed User-Agent string, matching known Koi Stealer check-in behavior.

## 3. Timeline (UTC)

- **17:32:31** — capture starts, normal domain/DHCP/DNS activity for DESKTOP-RNVO9AT.
- **17:35:04** — TLS session opens from 172.17.0.99 → **46.254.34.201:443**, SNI `www.bellantonicioccolato.it`, transferring ~701 KB encrypted. This immediately precedes infection and is the likely payload-delivery channel; content cannot be recovered since it's TLS-encrypted, so no file name/hash is available from it.
- **17:35:07** onward — repeated `POST /foots.php` beacons to **79.124.78.197:80**, roughly every 60–90 seconds, continuing for the remainder of the capture (through ~18:29, i.e. the full ~3576-second capture duration). 48 beacons total triggered the ET rule.
- **17:35:00** — `GET /index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U` to 79.124.78.197, server responded with `HckDcK0czXjaq48jVHNn|qIOuKk7U|http://79.124.78.197/index.php|` — an infection/campaign registration exchange (ID `qIOuKk7U` is the campaign/subaffiliate identifier).
- **17:35:01** — `POST /index.php` to 79.124.78.197 (registration follow-up).

## 4. Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoints:**
- `79.124.78.197:80` (HTTP) — primary Koi Stealer C2, confirmed by ET rule and beacon content
- `46.254.34.201:443` (TLS) — probable payload-delivery host, SNI-fronted

**Domains observed:**
- `www.bellantonicioccolato.it` (SNI value only, resolved to 46.254.34.201; no corresponding DNS query for this name was captured, consistent with a hardcoded/pre-resolved connection)

**Malicious URLs:**
- `http://79.124.78.197/foots.php` — C2 beacon/check-in endpoint (POST, repeated)
- `http://79.124.78.197/index.php` — registration endpoint (POST)
- `http://79.124.78.197/index.php?id=&subid=qIOuKk7U` — initial registration GET (subid `qIOuKk7U`)

**Transferred files / hashes:**
- None recoverable. All plaintext HTTP responses in the capture are `text/html`/`text/plain` (Microsoft connectivity/update checks, CRL/CTL downloads) — no binary object was transferred over unencrypted HTTP. The only large-volume transfer (~701 KB) is TLS-encrypted to 46.254.34.201, so no file name or SHA256 could be extracted from this capture.

## 5. Noise / Non-Findings

The alert export also flags SMB (`SMBv1`, `NTLMSSP unicode asn1 overflow`, `IPC$ unicode share access`), an SMB `TRANSACTION` DOS-attempt rule, and a Kerberos principal-name-overflow rule, all between 172.17.0.99 and the domain controller 172.17.0.17. Inspection of the actual SMB/NTLMSSP exchanges shows standard anonymous/NULL session domain browsing and normal Kerberos AS-REQ/AS-REP traffic for user `afletcher` — no exploit payload or overflow condition is present in the packet data. These are legacy GPL signatures known for false-positiving on ordinary Windows domain traffic and should not be treated as separate exploitation activity.
